title: ghrelease: HTTP client should be configurable or reusable
Critical: Attribute name mismatch between preprocessor and json-server backend
description: The Rust preprocessor generates data-comment-id attributes, but comments-json-server.js expects data-mdbook-comments-id. This means the json-server backend cannot find commentable paragraphs. The base comments.js uses data-comment-id which matches, but has different API structure than what tests expect. Either: (1) Change preprocessor to generate data-mdbook-comments-id for json-server backend, or (2) Change json-server JS to use data-comment-id, or (3) Make it configurable.

title: Technical debt: No unit tests for Rust preprocessor
description: The mdbook-comments preprocessor has zero Rust unit tests. Only e2e Playwright tests exist. Should add unit tests for: (1) Markdown parsing and block extraction, (2) Metadata generation including ID generation and hashing, (3) Comment link injection, (4) Asset injection. This would make it much easier to verify preprocessor behavior without running full mdbook builds and browser tests.

title: Technical debt: Duplicated code across 5 JavaScript backend implementations
description: There are 5 separate JS implementations (4336 total lines) with significant code duplication: comments.js (719 lines), comments-json-server.js (751 lines), comments-neon.js (988 lines), comments-supabase.js (804 lines), comments-googlesheets.js (1074 lines). Much of the UI rendering, fuzzy matching, DOM manipulation, and event handling is duplicated across all files. Should refactor to: (1) Extract common UI/matching logic into a shared module, (2) Create thin backend adapters that only handle API calls, (3) Use composition instead of duplication.

title: Technical debt: Asset injection bloats HTML by duplicating JS/CSS in every chapter
description: Currently CSS and JS are embedded inline in every chapter's HTML. For a book with N chapters, we duplicate the entire JavaScript (~1000 lines) and CSS N times. This bloats HTML files and prevents effective browser caching. Should instead: (1) Output JS/CSS as separate files in book output directory, (2) Inject <script src="..."  and <link rel="stylesheet"...> tags instead of inline code, or (3) Only inject into index.html and use shared layout. This would reduce HTML size significantly and improve caching.

title: Documentation: Missing instructions for selecting/configuring backend
description: README.md describes 4 backend options (Supabase, Neon, Google Sheets, Custom API) but doesn't explain how to actually configure which one to use. Users can see api-url in book.toml but there's no backend-type or similar setting documented. Need to either: (1) Document the expected configuration if it exists, or (2) Add the configuration mechanism if it doesn't exist, or (3) Document that users need to manually swap JS files (current workaround).

title: Investigate: Could we use mdbook's additional-js/additional-css with dynamically written files?
description: Currently we embed CSS/JS inline in every chapter's markdown (bloats HTML). Alternative approach: Write CSS/JS files to book's src directory during preprocessing, add them to book config's additional-js/additional-css arrays, then clean up after build. This would: (1) Keep single binary, (2) Let mdbook handle asset inclusion in all pages, (3) Enable browser caching. Trade-offs: (1) More complex, (2) Must handle cleanup, (3) Thread safety if multiple builds run. Worth investigating if it's cleaner than current inline approach.

title: Consider migrating frontend from vanilla JS to React or modern framework
description: Currently the frontend is written in vanilla JS with manual DOM manipulation (4336 total lines across 5 backend implementations). Consider migrating to React, Preact, or another modern framework for: (1) Better code organization and reusability, (2) Easier state management, (3) Simpler component composition instead of string concatenation, (4) Better TypeScript support, (5) Easier testing. Would need to handle embedding the built bundle into the Rust binary. Alternatively, could use a lighter approach like Preact or even just a build step for vanilla JS with better tooling.

title: Migrate JavaScript codebase to TypeScript
description: Currently all frontend code is vanilla JavaScript with no type safety. Migrating to TypeScript would provide: (1) Type safety and better IDE support, (2) Earlier error detection, (3) Better documentation through types, (4) Easier refactoring, (5) More maintainable codebase. Would need to: (1) Add TypeScript build step, (2) Convert .js files to .ts, (3) Add type definitions for DOM manipulation and API calls, (4) Update rust-embed to bundle the compiled JS. This could be done alongside or before the React migration (bd-366).

- Adds unnecessary complexity and maintenance burden
- No active users or deployment guides for Neon backend
- Other backends (json-server, supabase, google-sheets) are better options

title: Refactor remaining backend implementations to use base module
description:
After bd-362 refactored json-server to use the new base module architecture, the remaining backends need the same treatment:

Backends to refactor:
- comments-supabase.js (~800 lines) → comments-supabase-adapter.js (~100-150 lines)
- comments-googlesheets.js (~1,074 lines) → comments-googlesheets-adapter.js (~150-200 lines)  
- comments.js (custom backend, ~719 lines) → comments-custom-adapter.js (~100 lines)

Each adapter should:
- Implement the backend interface: init(), loadComments(), saveComment(), saveReply()
- Handle backend-specific authentication and API calls
- Normalize data formats to match base module expectations
- Be ~80-90% smaller than the original monolithic implementation

This will complete the code deduplication effort started in bd-362, eliminating another ~2,500 lines of duplicated code.

Dependencies: 
- bd-362 (completed - established the pattern)

Note: Do NOT refactor neon backend - it should be removed entirely (separate issue)
